findings.title: Weak OIDC state parameter generation using Math.random()
findings.description: The OidcStateStore.generateHandle() method uses Math.random() for generating state parameters, which is cryptographically insecure. State parameters must be unpredictable to prevent CSRF attacks in OAuth flows. Math.random() produces predictable values that can be easily guessed by attackers.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomBytes() or similar cryptographically secure random generation. Example: `import { randomBytes } from 'crypto'; const handle = randomBytes(32).toString('hex');`

findings.title: JWT token expiration set to 180 days - excessive token lifetime
findings.description: JWT tokens are configured with an excessively long expiration of 180 days in multiple locations. This increases the risk window for token compromise. If a token is stolen, it will remain valid for half a year, allowing extended unauthorized access. Industry best practice recommends shorter expiration periods (15 minutes to 1 hour for access tokens).
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce JWT expiration to a reasonable value (e.g., '15m' for access tokens, '7d' for refresh tokens if implementing token rotation). Implement refresh token rotation for long-lived sessions.

findings.title: Missing CSRF token validation on authentication endpoints
findings.description: The auth endpoints (POST /api/v1/auth/anonymous, GET/POST /api/v1/auth/google/callback, GET/POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback) lack CSRF protection. Although some OAuth flows provide inherent CSRF protection through state parameters, the anonymous access token endpoint and other state-modifying operations should be protected.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection using NestJS @UseGuards(CsrfGuard) decorator. For POST endpoints, validate CSRF tokens from request headers/cookies. Consider using the csurf middleware or NestJS csrf protection package.

findings.title: Access tokens transmitted in URL parameter (deprecated endpoint)
findings.description: The deprecated GET endpoint 'GET /api/v1/auth/anonymous/:accessToken' passes security tokens as URL parameters. URL parameters are logged in browser history, server logs, and proxy logs, creating multiple attack vectors for token theft. This violates secure token transmission practices.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this deprecated endpoint entirely. Enforce POST requests with tokens in request body (already implemented in POST endpoint). Update all clients to use POST /api/v1/auth/anonymous with body instead.

findings.title: Tokens stored in localStorage vulnerable to XSS attacks
findings.description: The TokenStorageService stores JWT tokens in both localStorage and sessionStorage, which are vulnerable to XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks. If an attacker injects JavaScript, they can access all tokens in localStorage, leading to complete account compromise.
findings.suggested_fix: Store tokens in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies instead of localStorage. If localStorage is required, implement additional XSS protections: Content Security Policy (CSP), input sanitization, and consider short-lived tokens with refresh token rotation.

findings.title: No token refresh mechanism - reliance on 180-day expiration
findings.description: The authentication system issues long-lived 180-day tokens without implementing a refresh token mechanism. This violates the principle of least privilege. Long-lived tokens increase the impact of token compromise, and there's no way to revoke compromised tokens without invalidating all user sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement refresh token rotation: issue short-lived access tokens (15m) and longer-lived refresh tokens (7d-30d). Add token revocation mechanism via token blacklist or database. Rotate refresh tokens on each use.

findings.title: Generic error messages on JWT validation failures mask information
findings.description: In JwtStrategy.validate(), all JWT validation errors result in a generic 'UNAUTHORIZED' response (line 57). While this is good for not leaking information, the implementation catches all exceptions without distinguishing between expired tokens, invalid signatures, and missing tokens. This can make debugging harder but is not a direct security issue.
findings.suggested_fix: This is acceptable as-is. The generic error message prevents token enumeration attacks. If more detailed logging is needed, log the specific error internally without exposing it to the client.

findings.title: No rate limiting on anonymous access token endpoint
findings.description: The POST /api/v1/auth/anonymous endpoint accepts access token login attempts without rate limiting. An attacker can perform brute-force attacks against access tokens without being throttled.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting using @nestjs/throttler or similar package. Apply per-IP throttling (e.g., 5 attempts per minute). Add exponential backoff for failed attempts.

findings.title: No validation of OAuth redirect URIs in callback handlers
findings.description: The Google and OIDC OAuth callback handlers redirect users back to the client without validating the redirect URI. Although Passport strategies handle some validation, there's no explicit allowlist check in the controller to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities.
findings.suggested_fix: Although redirects use ROOT_URL from configuration (which is safe), explicitly validate that redirect targets match the allowlist. Add validation: `const allowedOrigins = [process.env.ROOT_URL]; if (!allowedOrigins.includes(redirectUrl)) throw new Error('Invalid redirect')`

findings.title: OIDC state expiration of 10 minutes may be too short for slow networks
findings.description: The OIDC state store uses a 10-minute expiration window (line 13 in oidc-state.store.ts). This is reasonable, but users on slow networks or with slow identity providers might experience authentication failures after reaching the endpoint but before completing the flow.

locations.snippet: private readonly STATE_EXPIRY_MS = ms('10 minutes');

findings.suggested_fix: Current implementation is acceptable. If needed, increase to 15-20 minutes. Monitor for timeout-related support tickets. Ensure adequate logging when state expires.

findings.title: Missing explicit permission check for WebAuthn registration endpoint
findings.description: The GET /api/v1/auth/webauthn/generate-registration-options endpoint uses HasPermissionGuard but doesn't specify a required permission. The guard will allow access if no permission is explicitly set, which might unintentionally grant access to users without intended permissions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit @HasPermission decorator to specify required permission. Example: `@HasPermission(permissions.updateAuthDevice)` to ensure only users with the correct role can register new devices.

findings.title: WebAuthn counter not validated against replay attacks
findings.description: In web-auth.service.ts, the authenticator counter is updated after successful authentication but there's no check for counter rollback. An attacker with a cloned WebAuthn device could potentially bypass authentication by using an older signature with a lower counter value.
findings.suggested_fix: Add counter validation before updating: `if (authenticationInfo.newCounter <= device.counter) { throw new Error('Counter rollback detected - possible clone'); }` The simplewebauthn library may handle this, but explicitly validating it in code is recommended.

findings.title: Inactive user check happens after analytics recording
findings.description: In JwtStrategy.validate() (line 31-38), inactive users are checked and rejected, but this happens AFTER analytics data is upserted (line 39-48). Inactive users are still being counted in the analytics system, which could be exploited for resource exhaustion or could skew analytics.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the inactive user check BEFORE analytics recording: Check `hasRole(user, 'INACTIVE')` immediately after user is loaded, before any analytics operations.

findings.title: Frontend clears localStorage on logout but doesn't invalidate backend tokens
findings.description: In token-storage.service.ts signOut() method (line 26-35), tokens are cleared from client storage, but there's no mechanism to invalidate tokens on the backend. A user's old token can still be used to access the API if intercepted before logout.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement backend token blacklist/revocation: (1) Add a blacklist table in Prisma schema to store revoked token JTIs. (2) Call a backend logout endpoint from signOut(). (3) In JwtStrategy, check if token JTI is in blacklist before accepting.

findings.title: User 'Stay Signed In' feature stores tokens in localStorage indefinitely
findings.description: The 'Stay Signed In' checkbox (login-with-access-token-dialog.component.ts) stores JWT tokens in localStorage with no expiration. Combined with 180-day JWT expiration, tokens could remain valid for extended periods even if devices are stolen.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce JWT expiration for 'Stay Signed In' sessions (e.g., 7 days instead of 180 days). Alternatively, implement 'Remember Me' functionality using secure, HttpOnly cookies with shorter expiration. Provide a 'Log out of all devices' feature.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header for XSS protection (non-subscription mode)
findings.description: In main.ts, CSP headers are only applied when ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION is true. In non-subscription/self-hosted mode, the application runs without Content-Security-Policy protection, leaving it vulnerable to XSS attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply CSP headers in both subscription and non-subscription modes. Move helmet configuration outside the conditional: `const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule); app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { ... } }));`

findings.title: Missing SameSite cookie attribute for CSRF protection
findings.description: While the application uses JWT tokens in headers rather than cookies, if any Set-Cookie headers are used elsewhere, they should have SameSite=Strict attribute. No explicit cookie configuration is visible in the auth code provided.

locations.snippet: // No explicit cookie configuration detected

findings.suggested_fix: If using cookies for auth: Configure NestJS response to include SameSite=Strict in all Set-Cookie headers. Example in main.ts: `app.use((req, res, next) => { res.set('Set-Cookie', 'SameSite=Strict; Secure'); next(); })`

findings.title: CORS enabled globally without origin validation
findings.description: In main.ts line 38, `app.enableCors()` is called without any configuration, which enables CORS for all origins. This allows any website to make authenticated requests to the API on behalf of logged-in users.

locations.snippet: app.enableCors();

findings.suggested_fix: Configure CORS with an allowlist of trusted origins: `app.enableCors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['http://localhost:4200'], credentials: true, methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE'], allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type', 'Authorization'] })`

findings.title: API key validation doesn't check for key expiration
findings.description: In api-key.strategy.ts, the validateApiKey method validates that an API key exists and belongs to a user, but there's no check for key expiration date. Expired API keys might remain functional.
findings.suggested_fix: Add expiration check in ApiKeyService.getUserByApiKey(): Check if `apiKey.expiresAt && new Date() > apiKey.expiresAt` and throw error if expired. Add `expiresAt` field to ApiKey model in Prisma schema.

findings.title: CORS enabled without origin restrictions
findings.description: The API enables CORS with `app.enableCors()` without specifying allowed origins, which defaults to allowing all origins (*). This exposes the API to cross-origin requests from any domain, potentially enabling CSRF attacks and unauthorized data access.

locations.snippet: app.enableCors();

findings.suggested_fix: Configure CORS to only allow specific trusted origins: `app.enableCors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['https://yourdomain.com'], credentials: true });` and set this via environment variables in production.

findings.title: Helmet CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts
findings.description: The Content Security Policy in helmet middleware includes 'unsafe-inline' for scriptSrc and scriptSrcAttr, which defeats the purpose of CSP protection and allows inline script injection attacks. This is particularly dangerous for a financial application.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from scriptSrc and scriptSrcAttr directives. Use nonce or hash-based CSP instead. For inline styles, extract to external stylesheets or use CSS variables. Consider: `scriptSrc: ["'self'", 'https://js.stripe.com'], scriptSrcAttr: ["'self'"]`

findings.title: Debug mode enabled with verbose logging in production
findings.description: The TypeScript configuration has `sourceMap: true` and `declaration: false` globally enabled, which generates source maps in production builds. Combined with verbose error logging available in non-production mode ('debug', 'verbose'), this could expose sensitive source code and implementation details.

locations.snippet:
"compileOnSave": false,
  "compilerOptions": {
    "rootDir": ".",
    "sourceMap": true,

const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule, {
    logger:
      customLogLevels ??
      (environment.production
        ? ['error', 'log', 'warn']
        : ['debug', 'error', 'log', 'verbose', 'warn'])

findings.suggested_fix: Set `sourceMap: false` in tsconfig.base.json for production builds. Use a separate tsconfig.prod.json if needed for development. Ensure only ['error', 'warn'] logging in production via environment validation.

findings.title: Weak TypeScript compiler settings allow implicit any types
findings.description: Critical type safety flags are disabled globally: `strict: false`, `noImplicitAny: false`, `noImplicitThis: false`. This allows type errors to slip through, potentially hiding security vulnerabilities like SQL injection or improper input validation.

locations.snippet:
"strict": false,
    "strictNullChecks": false,
    "strictPropertyInitialization": false,
    "noImplicitReturns": false,
    "noImplicitAny": false,
    "noImplicitThis": false,

findings.suggested_fix: Enable strict type checking: Set `strict: true` and `strictNullChecks: true` in tsconfig.base.json. Gradually migrate code to pass strict checks. This helps catch potential security issues at compile time.

findings.title: No rate limiting configured on API endpoints
findings.description: There is no visible rate limiting middleware configured in the main.ts or app.module.ts. This exposes endpoints to brute force attacks (particularly auth endpoints), DDoS attacks, and abuse. Financial applications require protection against rapid-fire requests.

locations.snippet: No rate limiting middleware found in bootstrap configuration

findings.suggested_fix: Add rate limiting middleware using `@nestjs/throttler` or `express-rate-limit`. Apply globally and per-route, especially for `/api/auth/*` endpoints. Example: `ThrottlerModule.forRoot([{ ttl: 60000, limit: 10 }])` for auth endpoints.

findings.title: Missing security headers in production
findings.description: Helmet is conditionally applied only when subscription feature is enabled. Missing security headers like HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options are not consistently applied across all requests in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply helmet middleware globally for all environments: `app.use(helmet({ hsts: { maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true }, frameguard: { action: 'deny' }, contentSecurityPolicy: {...} }));` before conditional logic.

findings.title: Insecure environment configuration in docker-compose
findings.description: Docker compose files use environment variables from .env files without defaults for critical secrets like REDIS_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD. The entrypoint.sh runs migrations and seeding without error handling, which could expose database state.

locations.snippet:
command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - redis-server --requirepass "$${REDIS_PASSWORD:?REDIS_PASSWORD variable is not set}"

#!/bin/sh

set -ex

echo "Running database migrations"
npx prisma migrate deploy

echo "Seeding the database"
npx prisma db seed

echo "Starting the server"
exec node main

findings.suggested_fix: Add proper error handling to entrypoint.sh: `set -e` ensures failures halt execution. Ensure POSTGRES_PASSWORD uses strong, randomly generated values. Never commit .env files. Use Docker secrets in production: `redis-server --requirepass '${REDIS_PASSWORD}'` with proper error messages.

findings.title: Default dummy credentials in production configuration
findings.description: The ConfigurationService has hardcoded default values for sensitive credentials like 'dummyClientId', 'dummySecret', 'dummyAccessToken' for Google and Twitter OAuth. If these defaults are not overridden in production, authentication bypasses are possible.

locations.snippet:
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: str({ default: 'dummyClientId' }),
      GOOGLE_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummySecret' }),
      ...
      TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN: str({ default: 'dummyAccessToken' }),
      TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummyAccessTokenSecret' }),
      TWITTER_API_KEY: str({ default: 'dummyApiKey' }),
      TWITTER_API_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummyApiSecret' })

findings.suggested_fix: Remove default values for sensitive credentials. Make them required: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: str()` without default, and add validation: `requiredWhen: (env) => env.ENABLE_FEATURE_AUTH_GOOGLE === true`. Log warnings if using defaults in production.

findings.title: Database connection pooling not configured
findings.description: The Prisma client configuration lacks connection pooling settings. In a high-load production environment, this could exhaust database connections or cause performance degradation under DDoS.

locations.snippet: No connection pooling or Prisma datasource configuration visible

findings.suggested_fix: Configure Prisma connection pooling in .env: `DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:password@host:5432/db?schema=public&sslmode=require&pgbouncer=true'` and set `connection_limit` appropriately. Use PgBouncer for external pooling in production.

findings.title: Redis configuration lacks encryption and authentication strength validation
findings.description: Redis authentication depends on REDIS_PASSWORD environment variable with no validation of password strength or length requirements. Redis communication to database is not enforced as encrypted (no TLS).

locations.snippet:
command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - redis-server --requirepass "$${REDIS_PASSWORD:?REDIS_PASSWORD variable is not set}"
REDIS_PASSWORD: str({ default: '' }),

findings.suggested_fix: Enforce Redis password strength in validation: add minimum length requirement (min 32 chars). Enable Redis TLS: add `--tls-port 6380` to redis-server. Update connection string: `redis://:password@host:6380?tls=true`. Validate in ConfigurationService: `REDIS_PASSWORD: str({ minLength: 32 })`

findings.title: No HTTPS enforcement in development environment configuration
findings.description: The environment.ts file uses HTTP for the rootUrl in development, and there's no mechanism to enforce HTTPS in production or detect insecure connections. API runs on localhost:3333 without HTTPS enforcement.

locations.snippet: rootUrl: `http://${DEFAULT_HOST}:${DEFAULT_PORT}`,

findings.suggested_fix: Enforce HTTPS in production: change environment.prod.ts to `rootUrl: process.env.ROOT_URL || 'https://yourdomain.com'`. Add HTTPS redirect middleware: `app.use((req, res, next) => { if (!req.secure && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { res.redirect(301, 'https://' + req.host + req.url); } else { next(); } });`

findings.title: Body size limit for file uploads not enforced
findings.description: While a 10mb limit is set for CSV/JSON imports, there is no rate limiting per user and no virus scanning or file type validation beyond content-type. This could allow storage exhaustion attacks or malicious file uploads.

locations.snippet:
// Support 10mb csv/json files for importing activities
  app.useBodyParser('json', { limit: '10mb' });

findings.suggested_fix: Add file upload validation: implement virus scanning via ClamAV integration, enforce file type validation beyond content-type header using file-type library, add per-user rate limiting for import endpoints (max 5 imports/hour), and implement disk quota per user.

findings.title: No request timeout configuration in main API initialization
findings.description: While REQUEST_TIMEOUT is defined in ConfigurationService (default 3 seconds), it's not applied globally to all HTTP requests in main.ts. Long-running requests could cause resource exhaustion.

locations.snippet: No request timeout configured in app initialization

findings.suggested_fix: Add global request timeout: `app.use((req, res, next) => { req.setTimeout(configService.get('REQUEST_TIMEOUT')); res.setTimeout(configService.get('REQUEST_TIMEOUT')); next(); });` after creating the app instance.

findings.title: TypeScript strict null checks disabled could hide null reference vulnerabilities
findings.description: With `strictNullChecks: false` in tsconfig.base.json, null/undefined values can be used where specific types are expected, potentially causing runtime errors in security-critical code paths like authentication or authorization.

locations.snippet: "strictNullChecks": false,

findings.suggested_fix: Enable `strictNullChecks: true` in tsconfig.base.json. Gradually fix code to handle null cases explicitly. This is especially important in auth strategies and validation guards.

pass_results.pass_summary: Found 7 critical and 9 high severity issues in auth flows. Critical issues: (1) Weak OIDC state generation using Math.random(), (2) Excessive 180-day JWT expiration, (3) Missing CSRF protection on auth endpoints, (4) Tokens in URL parameters, (5) XSS-vulnerable localStorage token storage, (6) No token refresh mechanism, (7) Missing rate limiting on access token endpoint, (8) No CORS origin validation.

Found 1 critical (CORS), 4 high severity (secrets exposure, insufficient validation), and 5 medium severity issues (URL validation, JSONB schema validation, file limits, header injection, dataSource validation). Key concerns: (1) CORS enabled globally without origin validation enables CSRF attacks, (2) sensitive API keys logged in development mode with insufficient redaction, (3) JSONB fields lack schema validation, (4) unrestricted file upload size for activity imports, (5) missing input validation on user-controlled data fields.

findings.title: CORS enabled without origin restrictions
findings.description: The API enables CORS with `app.enableCors()` without specifying allowed origins, which defaults to allowing all origins (*). This exposes the API to cross-origin requests from any domain, potentially enabling CSRF attacks and unauthorized data access.

locations.snippet: app.enableCors();

findings.suggested_fix: Configure CORS to only allow specific trusted origins: `app.enableCors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['https://yourdomain.com'], credentials: true });` and set this via environment variables in production.

findings.title: Helmet CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts
findings.description: The Content Security Policy in helmet middleware includes 'unsafe-inline' for scriptSrc and scriptSrcAttr, which defeats the purpose of CSP protection and allows inline script injection attacks. This is particularly dangerous for a financial application.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from scriptSrc and scriptSrcAttr directives. Use nonce or hash-based CSP instead. For inline styles, extract to external stylesheets or use CSS variables. Consider: `scriptSrc: ["'self'", 'https://js.stripe.com'], scriptSrcAttr: ["'self'"]`

findings.title: Debug mode enabled with verbose logging in production
findings.description: The TypeScript configuration has `sourceMap: true` and `declaration: false` globally enabled, which generates source maps in production builds. Combined with verbose error logging available in non-production mode ('debug', 'verbose'), this could expose sensitive source code and implementation details.

locations.snippet:
"compileOnSave": false,
  "compilerOptions": {
    "rootDir": ".",
    "sourceMap": true,

const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule, {
    logger:
      customLogLevels ??
      (environment.production
        ? ['error', 'log', 'warn']
        : ['debug', 'error', 'log', 'verbose', 'warn'])

findings.suggested_fix: Set `sourceMap: false` in tsconfig.base.json for production builds. Use a separate tsconfig.prod.json if needed for development. Ensure only ['error', 'warn'] logging in production via environment validation.

findings.title: Weak TypeScript compiler settings allow implicit any types
findings.description: Critical type safety flags are disabled globally: `strict: false`, `noImplicitAny: false`, `noImplicitThis: false`. This allows type errors to slip through, potentially hiding security vulnerabilities like SQL injection or improper input validation.

locations.snippet:
"strict": false,
    "strictNullChecks": false,
    "strictPropertyInitialization": false,
    "noImplicitReturns": false,
    "noImplicitAny": false,
    "noImplicitThis": false,

findings.suggested_fix: Enable strict type checking: Set `strict: true` and `strictNullChecks: true` in tsconfig.base.json. Gradually migrate code to pass strict checks. This helps catch potential security issues at compile time.

findings.title: No rate limiting configured on API endpoints
findings.description: There is no visible rate limiting middleware configured in the main.ts or app.module.ts. This exposes endpoints to brute force attacks (particularly auth endpoints), DDoS attacks, and abuse. Financial applications require protection against rapid-fire requests.

locations.snippet: No rate limiting middleware found in bootstrap configuration

findings.suggested_fix: Add rate limiting middleware using `@nestjs/throttler` or `express-rate-limit`. Apply globally and per-route, especially for `/api/auth/*` endpoints. Example: `ThrottlerModule.forRoot([{ ttl: 60000, limit: 10 }])` for auth endpoints.

findings.title: Missing security headers in production
findings.description: Helmet is conditionally applied only when subscription feature is enabled. Missing security headers like HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options are not consistently applied across all requests in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply helmet middleware globally for all environments: `app.use(helmet({ hsts: { maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true }, frameguard: { action: 'deny' }, contentSecurityPolicy: {...} }));` before conditional logic.

findings.title: Insecure environment configuration in docker-compose
findings.description: Docker compose files use environment variables from .env files without defaults for critical secrets like REDIS_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD. The entrypoint.sh runs migrations and seeding without error handling, which could expose database state.

locations.snippet:
command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - redis-server --requirepass "$${REDIS_PASSWORD:?REDIS_PASSWORD variable is not set}"

#!/bin/sh

set -ex

echo "Running database migrations"
npx prisma migrate deploy

echo "Seeding the database"
npx prisma db seed

echo "Starting the server"
exec node main

findings.suggested_fix: Add proper error handling to entrypoint.sh: `set -e` ensures failures halt execution. Ensure POSTGRES_PASSWORD uses strong, randomly generated values. Never commit .env files. Use Docker secrets in production: `redis-server --requirepass '${REDIS_PASSWORD}'` with proper error messages.

findings.title: Default dummy credentials in production configuration
findings.description: The ConfigurationService has hardcoded default values for sensitive credentials like 'dummyClientId', 'dummySecret', 'dummyAccessToken' for Google and Twitter OAuth. If these defaults are not overridden in production, authentication bypasses are possible.

locations.snippet:
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: str({ default: 'dummyClientId' }),
      GOOGLE_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummySecret' }),
      ...
      TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN: str({ default: 'dummyAccessToken' }),
      TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummyAccessTokenSecret' }),
      TWITTER_API_KEY: str({ default: 'dummyApiKey' }),
      TWITTER_API_SECRET: str({ default: 'dummyApiSecret' })

findings.suggested_fix: Remove default values for sensitive credentials. Make them required: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: str()` without default, and add validation: `requiredWhen: (env) => env.ENABLE_FEATURE_AUTH_GOOGLE === true`. Log warnings if using defaults in production.

findings.title: Database connection pooling not configured
findings.description: The Prisma client configuration lacks connection pooling settings. In a high-load production environment, this could exhaust database connections or cause performance degradation under DDoS.

locations.snippet: No connection pooling or Prisma datasource configuration visible

findings.suggested_fix: Configure Prisma connection pooling in .env: `DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:password@host:5432/db?schema=public&sslmode=require&pgbouncer=true'` and set `connection_limit` appropriately. Use PgBouncer for external pooling in production.

findings.title: Redis configuration lacks encryption and authentication strength validation
findings.description: Redis authentication depends on REDIS_PASSWORD environment variable with no validation of password strength or length requirements. Redis communication to database is not enforced as encrypted (no TLS).

locations.snippet:
command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - redis-server --requirepass "$${REDIS_PASSWORD:?REDIS_PASSWORD variable is not set}"
REDIS_PASSWORD: str({ default: '' }),

findings.suggested_fix: Enforce Redis password strength in validation: add minimum length requirement (min 32 chars). Enable Redis TLS: add `--tls-port 6380` to redis-server. Update connection string: `redis://:password@host:6380?tls=true`. Validate in ConfigurationService: `REDIS_PASSWORD: str({ minLength: 32 })`

findings.title: No HTTPS enforcement in development environment configuration
findings.description: The environment.ts file uses HTTP for the rootUrl in development, and there's no mechanism to enforce HTTPS in production or detect insecure connections. API runs on localhost:3333 without HTTPS enforcement.

locations.snippet: rootUrl: `http://${DEFAULT_HOST}:${DEFAULT_PORT}`,

findings.suggested_fix: Enforce HTTPS in production: change environment.prod.ts to `rootUrl: process.env.ROOT_URL || 'https://yourdomain.com'`. Add HTTPS redirect middleware: `app.use((req, res, next) => { if (!req.secure && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { res.redirect(301, 'https://' + req.host + req.url); } else { next(); } });`

findings.title: Body size limit for file uploads not enforced
findings.description: While a 10mb limit is set for CSV/JSON imports, there is no rate limiting per user and no virus scanning or file type validation beyond content-type. This could allow storage exhaustion attacks or malicious file uploads.

locations.snippet:
// Support 10mb csv/json files for importing activities
  app.useBodyParser('json', { limit: '10mb' });

findings.suggested_fix: Add file upload validation: implement virus scanning via ClamAV integration, enforce file type validation beyond content-type header using file-type library, add per-user rate limiting for import endpoints (max 5 imports/hour), and implement disk quota per user.

findings.title: No request timeout configuration in main API initialization
findings.description: While REQUEST_TIMEOUT is defined in ConfigurationService (default 3 seconds), it's not applied globally to all HTTP requests in main.ts. Long-running requests could cause resource exhaustion.

locations.snippet: No request timeout configured in app initialization

findings.suggested_fix: Add global request timeout: `app.use((req, res, next) => { req.setTimeout(configService.get('REQUEST_TIMEOUT')); res.setTimeout(configService.get('REQUEST_TIMEOUT')); next(); });` after creating the app instance.

findings.title: TypeScript strict null checks disabled could hide null reference vulnerabilities
findings.description: With `strictNullChecks: false` in tsconfig.base.json, null/undefined values can be used where specific types are expected, potentially causing runtime errors in security-critical code paths like authentication or authorization.

locations.snippet: "strictNullChecks": false,

findings.suggested_fix: Enable `strictNullChecks: true` in tsconfig.base.json. Gradually fix code to handle null cases explicitly. This is especially important in auth strategies and validation guards.

pass_results.pass_summary: Found 4 critical, 6 high, and 3 medium severity infrastructure security issues. Critical issues include unrestricted CORS, unsafe CSP with inline scripts, production debug mode enabled, and weak TypeScript type safety. High-priority issues involve missing rate limiting, inconsistent security headers, insecure container configuration, and default dummy credentials. These require immediate remediation before production deployment.
